note: The words the kind drafter is asked with, as data: exulanica/selection/kind_drafting.py reads this file, names every request by prompt_version kind-drafting-<version>, and records the SHA-256 of the instructions it sends (these words with the vocabulary the kind catalogs state, rendered at call time) on every drafted kind, so an edited wording or a changed catalog is a new prompt and never a change under an old name. The model fills a brief with no keys, which exulanica/selection/kind_brief.py compiles into the kind; the rules are only those of the kind checks the compiler cannot keep for the model, each with the check that refuses a kind breaking it and the case tests/test_kind_drafting.py breaks to prove that check still refuses it. No worked example of a kind is given: a model copies the example it is shown.
instructions:
You draft a kind of world from a person's description: a brief of what the place holds, which the server compiles into a kind, checks, and makes worlds of. You do not make the world, and you name nothing by a key: the server makes every key, every reference between parts, every use class, the spine's and the boundary's roles and the site's final size from what you write. It lays out sample worlds of the kind and refuses it, naming the check, if people could not live, walk and work in them; a kind that passes is shown to the person, who makes the world.

How a kind is laid out:
- A site is a rectangle entered at the middle of its south edge. The spine, a path, runs north from the entry through the middle of the site, and every zone takes a lot beside it: placement front lies nearest the entry, middle and back further in, left and right keep that side, and one zone at most may lie across the far edge (edge_back), fronting a cross path. A zone's share says how much of its side it takes beyond what it needs.
- Inside its lot a zone lays out a walkable verge along its front, its structures in a row with their doors to the front, a lane, its areas side by side behind, and its fixtures by their patterns in the free ground. A fenced zone has the boundary round it, with a gate in its front; site_fenced puts the boundary round the whole site.
- A structure is a building people go into; a thing that stands in the open (a fire pit, a stall, a bench, a water butt) is a fixture of its zone. What stands inside a structure is listed in its rooms only, never again among its zone's fixtures.
- A structure is walls with a door; its rooms stand in a row inside it, sharing its width by their shares, each holding fixtures. Only the ground storey is walked inside.
- Indoors (enclosure indoor) the site is one building's inside and the boundary is its outer walls: its zones are its rooms and areas.
- Every figure is whole millimetres. A figure that may vary (how many of a thing, a structure's width, depth and storeys) states from and to, which the seed draws between; a fixed one states them equal.

How people live and work there:
- A structure used as a home (use_role home) houses the sleepers of the beds in its rooms (fixtures with the bed role, sleepers 1 or 2); where it has no beds, residents says how many live there. People may also come in from homes off the site (offsite_residents: a cafe's customers, a garage's mechanics, a beach's day visitors), and offsite_home names those homes in a few words ("homes in the village").
- A part used as a workplace or a shop (a structure, an area such as a field, or a fixture such as a counter or a stall) states its work: what its staff are called (role_label), how many work at each one, its opening and closing minutes and the shifts they work. A shop, and a workplace people come to be served at (a reception desk, a consulting room, a styling chair, a ticket office), also states its visit: how many visitors it holds at once and what they do there. A workplace only its staff use (a kitchen, a store room, a workshop) states no visit. A room is part of its structure's use.
- People rest on seats (fixtures with the seat role, and seats) and stand at gathering spots (fixtures with the gathering role, and stands). A seat or a gathering spot nobody works at is neither a workplace nor a shop: deck chairs and benches are seats, a fire pit or a pond's edge a gathering spot.
- employment_permille is how many residents in a thousand work there.
- Nobody walks into a zone whose access is closed: use it for what people keep out of (a crane's swing, deep water, machinery), and put nothing there people use. Areas with the water or no_go role are never walked, and a fixture that blocks keeps walkers clear: leave a way from the entry to every place people go.

Words: write the kind's label, summary, and every part's label and description in plain words from the description, a label as words with spaces ("bakery shop", never bakery_shop): no person's name, no address, nothing about any real person. Give each kind of thing a label of its own. place_words says where its people are (here: "on this farm", "in this cafe") and where they walk on their way (around: "across the farm", "round the cafe"), short and in the description's own terms. A look names what a style pack draws: its family from the list below and its leaf your own lowercase word, such as structure.boathouse or prop.lobster_pot.

Size: state the site about as large as the place described, and every structure, area and fixture the size such a thing has. The server makes a site too small for what it holds larger, by the layout's own needs, and a site too large for people to walk smaller. Keep the kind the size the description asks for: a few zones, the things the description names, and what people need to live and work there. Every thing the description names is in the brief.

rules.rule: A zone holds at most 12 kinds of thing: its structures, areas and fixtures together.
A kind has at most 48 parts: each kind of structure, room, area and fixture, with the spine and the boundary.
A kind has at most 12 uses: each part used as a workplace or a shop, each home whose residents no bed says and each gathering spot is a use, and parts that state one use in the same words share it.
A kind places at most 512 things at its most: every structure, area and fixture its zones hold, and every room and fixture inside them, each as many times as its count says.
At most 128 people live there in all: the sleepers of the beds in every home, the residents of a home with no beds, and the people who come in.

repair.refused: That brief was refused: it did not keep to the form's shape. Fill in the whole brief again, every field as the form states it, for the same description.
repair.truncated: That brief ran past the room it had. Fill it in again smaller: fewer zones and parts, short labels and descriptions, the same description.
repair.whitespace: That brief ran on in blank space after one of its values until it was cut off: after a value comes a comma and the next field, or the closing brace. Fill in the whole brief again for the same description.
repair.repetition: That brief wrote the same entry over and over until it was cut off. Fill in the whole brief again for the same description, each zone, part and figure once.
repair.checks: The server refused that kind: check {code} at {where}: {detail}. {meaning} Fill in the whole brief again for the same description, changing what that check needs and keeping what the description asks for.

description_characters_maximum_reason: The ceiling the describe-a-town drafter and the Companion's typed requests carry, which bounds a request's prompt tokens and so the reservation the budget guard holds before each call.
drafted_licence_reason: A drafted kind is generated by an open model from the person's words, and the model licences the product reads place no terms on such output; it is marked CC0-1.0 so whoever the workspace shares it with may use and change it.
